SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which direction lies between south and east? (1 mark)
   A. North-east
   B. South-west
   C. North-west
   D. South-east

2. Which imaginary line crosses Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The river line
   B. The railway line
   C. The boundary
   D. The equator

3. County X covers 8 grid squares and County Y covers 5 grid squares. Which statement is correct? (1 mark)
   A. We cannot compare them
   B. County X is bigger than County Y
   C. They are the same size
   D. County Y is bigger than County X

4. Which of these is built by people, not natural? (1 mark)
   A. A dam
   B. A hill
   C. A plain
   D. A river

5. Which of these is a physical feature? (1 mark)
   A. A school
   B. A lake
   C. A bridge
   D. A road

6. Which physical feature helps people to catch fish? (1 mark)
   A. A lake
   B. A hill
   C. A plain
   D. A plateau

7. Which season usually follows the long rains in Kenya's common pattern? (1 mark)
   A. Cool or cold season
   B. Short rains
   C. Hot season
   D. Long rains again

8. During which season do fishermen often dry fish in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Dry season
   B. Flood season
   C. Rainy season
   D. No season

9. Which is a very old town on the Kenyan coast with narrow streets and stone houses? (1 mark)
   A. Thimlich Ohinga
   B. Eldoret
   C. Nakuru
   D. Lamu Old Town

10. In a chart of who gives and who needs, what does a farmer give? (1 mark)
   A. Transport
   B. Health care
   C. Learning
   D. Food

11. How is money useful in trade? (1 mark)
   A. It grows crops
   B. It makes buying and selling easier
   C. It builds houses
   D. It stops trade

12. In a shaded map, which shade usually shows the most crowded area? (1 mark)
   A. White
   B. The lightest shade
   C. No shade
   D. The darkest shade

13. In traditional culture, what do we call a basket or clay pot made and used by people? (1 mark)
   A. A type of weather
   B. A river
   C. An artefact
   D. A kind of food

14. What is culture? (1 mark)
   A. The way of life of a community
   B. A kind of weather
   C. A kind of animal
   D. A type of road

15. What is a gallery walk? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of assembly
   B. A cooking lesson
   C. Walking round to look at displayed work
   D. A race

16. What are values? (1 mark)
   A. Kinds of money
   B. Types of buildings
   C. Good beliefs that guide our behaviour
   D. Kinds of food

17. Which activity involves growing crops and keeping animals? (1 mark)
   A. Tourism
   B. Farming
   C. Mining
   D. Fishing

18. How do economic activities help a county government? (1 mark)
   A. They stop roads
   B. They cause drought
   C. Businesses pay taxes and fees
   D. They close clinics

19. What is an economic activity? (1 mark)
   A. A game after school
   B. A song
   C. A holiday
   D. Work done to earn income or make goods and services

20. Which is a service industry? (1 mark)
   A. A dairy plant
   B. A cement plant
   C. A sugar mill
   D. A hotel

21. Who should handle sharp tools in a school project? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody
   B. A young child alone
   C. An adult
   D. A visitor

22. Which of these is a quality of a good citizen in school? (1 mark)
   A. Bullying
   B. Cheating
   C. Honesty
   D. Laziness

23. Whose fault is it if a child is abused? (1 mark)
   A. The neighbour
   B. The child
   C. The abuser, never the child
   D. The teacher only

24. Which of these is a democratic process in school? (1 mark)
   A. A bully choosing leaders
   B. Electing a class monitor by voting
   C. Punishing pupils who speak
   D. Ignoring pupils' ideas

25. Which shows respect for the minority? (1 mark)
   A. Listening to those who did not win
   B. Laughing at them
   C. Ignoring them
   D. Sending them away

26. Who writes down what is discussed and decided at a meeting? (1 mark)
   A. The patron
   B. The president
   C. The Speaker
   D. The secretary

27. How can you show respect for community leaders? (1 mark)
   A. Insult them
   B. Listen politely and follow fair rules
   C. Spread rumours
   D. Refuse to attend meetings

28. Which quality means treating everyone equally? (1 mark)
   A. Selfishness
   B. Greed
   C. Boasting
   D. Fairness

29. Who leads the meetings of the county assembly? (1 mark)
   A. The chief
   B. The governor
   C. The Speaker
   D. The driver

30. What is a duty of an MCA? (1 mark)
   A. Command the army
   B. Represent the people of the ward in the assembly
   C. Issue passports
   D. Run national hospitals

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Name the five countries that border Kenya. (5 marks)

32. Name the three main kinds of historic built environments. (3 marks)

33. Give four services provided by county governments. (4 marks)

34. Explain why we should be honest even when nobody is watching. (3 marks)

35. Give four qualities of a good pupil leader. (4 marks)

36. State three functions of the Children's Government. (3 marks)

37. State three duties of a village elder. (3 marks)

38. Explain what may happen if people cut down all the trees on a mountain. (3 marks)

39. Name three natural resources found in Kenya and say how each is used. (3 marks)

40. Give five people who serve your community and say how each helps. (5 marks)

41. Describe how health workers, farmers and teachers depend on each other. (4 marks)

42. Name three child rights. (3 marks)

43. Explain how you can stay calm when you feel very angry. (3 marks)

44. Explain the meaning of population distribution. (2 marks)

45. Give two reasons why we obey school rules. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — South-east
   South-east is half way between south and east.

2. D — The equator
   The equator crosses the middle of Kenya.

3. B — County X is bigger than County Y
   8 squares is more land than 5 squares.

4. A — A dam
   A dam is built by people to hold water.

5. B — A lake
   A lake is natural. The others are built by people.

6. A — A lake
   People fish in lakes, rivers and the ocean.

7. A — Cool or cold season
   In the usual pattern, June to August is cool or cold in many places.

8. A — Dry season
   Dry sunny days are best for drying fish.

9. D — Lamu Old Town
   Lamu Old Town is one of the oldest towns on the coast.

10. D — Food
   Farmers give food to the community.

11. B — It makes buying and selling easier
   Money is a common way of paying for goods and services.

12. D — The darkest shade
   Dark shades show higher numbers.

13. C — An artefact
   Baskets and pots are artefacts.

14. A — The way of life of a community
   Culture is the way of life passed on from generation to generation.

15. C — Walking round to look at displayed work
   In a gallery walk pupils look at each other's displays.

16. C — Good beliefs that guide our behaviour
   Values guide how we behave.

17. B — Farming
   Farming is growing crops and keeping livestock.

18. C — Businesses pay taxes and fees
   Taxes and fees help pay for services.

19. D — Work done to earn income or make goods and services
   Economic activities bring in income.

20. D — A hotel
   Hotels provide services.

21. C — An adult
   Adults must handle dangerous tools.

22. C — Honesty
   Honesty is a positive quality.

23. C — The abuser, never the child
   Abuse is never the child's fault.

24. B — Electing a class monitor by voting
   Voting gives everyone a say.

25. A — Listening to those who did not win
   Democracy includes everyone.

26. D — The secretary
   The secretary keeps the minutes.

27. B — Listen politely and follow fair rules
   Respect means polite listening and obeying good rules.

28. D — Fairness
   Fair leaders treat all equally.

29. C — The Speaker
   The Speaker leads the assembly.

30. B — Represent the people of the ward in the assembly
   MCAs represent their wards.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: Uganda, Tanzania, Ethiopia, South Sudan and Somalia.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each country.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Museums, monuments and cultural centres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct kind.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Health centres, county roads, pre-primary schools and markets. Accept cattle dips or water services.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each service.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty builds trust, it is right, and it prepares us to be good citizens.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Honest, fair, responsible and a good listener. Accept humble or hard working.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Represent pupils, help keep order, and promote cleanliness. Accept organising activities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each function.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Welcome visitors, settle small quarrels and call meetings. Accept reporting problems.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rain may wash away the soil. Rivers may dry up. There may be landslides or floods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct result.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Water is used for drinking and farming. Land is used for farming and grazing. Minerals such as soda ash are used in factories.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each resource with a use.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example: farmer grows food, teacher teaches, nurse treats the sick, driver carries people and goods, trader sells goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each person with a correct service.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Health workers keep farmers and teachers well. Farmers give food to health workers and teachers. Teachers teach the children of farmers and health workers. Each group needs the others to live well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct link.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: The right to education, to health care and to protection. Accept food, a name or play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each right.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Walk away, take slow deep breaths, and count to ten before speaking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is how the people are spread out over an area, showing where many people live and where few live.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for spread of people, 1 mark for many and few.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Rules keep everyone safe and they help everyone to learn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.
